syllabus_topics: Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs): examples of solvable first-order ODEs, integrating factors
Existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence of solutions for first-order ODE systems
Laplace transform and applications to ODEs
Gauss and Stokes theorems and introduction to Partial Differential Equations (PDEs): surfaces in R^3
Surface integrals of scalar and vector fields
Divergence and curl of vector fields
Derivation of continuity, wave, heat, Laplace and Poisson differential equations
PDEs and Fourier series: linear 1st order PDEs
Wave, heat, Laplace and Poisson equations
Solutions of wave, heat, Laplace and Poisson equations, via separation of variables and Fourier series
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of 3 MAP45 tests (T), yielding an arithmetic mean. There is one 2-hour resit exam (E), or students can choose to retake one of the MAP45 tests. If at most 1 test is submitted and the exam is not submitted, the final grade is "NA". If the maximum of T and E is less than 9.5, the final grade is "RE". If the maximum of T and E is between 9.5 and 17.5, the final grade is the maximum of T and E. For students with a grade not less than 17.5, there will be an oral defense, and the final grade will be the grade obtained in this oral. Enrollment for each test is mandatory, and no calculators or consultation materials are allowed. Grades from previous enrollments do not count. The special period consists of a 2-hour exam, counting 100% for the final grade.
